title: The Age of AI
subtitle: And Our Human Future
pitch: A statesman, a former Google CEO and an MIT dean ask what AI means for knowledge, security, world order and what it is to be human.

chapters.g: Opens with AlphaZero and a new antibiotic found by AI, showing machines finding things humans could not.

chapters.t: How We Got Here: Technology and Human Thought
chapters.g: A history of how people understood reality, from faith to reason, and how AI adds a third way of knowing.

chapters.t: From Turing to Today, and Beyond
chapters.g: How AI developed, from Turing's test to machine learning, and what it can and cannot do.
How AI powered platforms like search and social media shape what billions of people see and think.
AI in weapons and cyber conflict, and why arms control ideas from the nuclear age need updating.
What happens to human self-understanding when machines reason in ways we cannot follow.
A call for leaders and societies to think deeply about AI before it reshapes them.

ideas: AI is a new way of knowing, beside faith and reason.
Platforms shape human thought at huge scale.
AI changes security and needs new arms control thinking.
We need philosophy, not just engineering.

args.a: AI will change how humans understand reality.
args.c: Critics say the book is long on big ideas and short on concrete safety proposals.

questions: Do you agree that AI is a new way of knowing?
How should countries do arms control for AI?

quiz.q: Which AI system opens the book?
quiz.w: AlphaZero's chess shows machines finding new strategies.
A statesman, a former Google CEO and an MIT dean.
